Badge

Badges are small, lightweight indicators for counts, states and labels. They scale to match the parent element and come in a full set of contextual colors.

Basic Badge

The default badge uses a neutral gray color scheme.

Default 42
HTML
<span class="zak-badge">Default</span>
<span class="zak-badge">42</span>

Color Variants

Use contextual variants to convey meaning.

Secondary Primary Success Danger Warning Info
HTML
<span class="zak-badge">Secondary</span>
<span class="zak-badge zak-badge-primary">Primary</span>
<span class="zak-badge zak-badge-success">Success</span>
<span class="zak-badge zak-badge-danger">Danger</span>
<span class="zak-badge zak-badge-warning">Warning</span>
<span class="zak-badge zak-badge-info">Info</span>

Pill Badge

Badges already use fully rounded corners. The .zak-badge-pill class is provided for semantic clarity and future overrides.

New In stock Sold out
HTML
<span class="zak-badge zak-badge-pill zak-badge-primary">New</span>
<span class="zak-badge zak-badge-pill zak-badge-success">In stock</span>
<span class="zak-badge zak-badge-pill zak-badge-danger">Sold out</span>

Badge on Buttons

Place badges inside buttons with a small gap on the text.

HTML
<button class="zak-btn zak-btn-primary">
  Notifications
  <span class="zak-badge zak-badge-light" style="margin-left: 0.35rem;">4</span>
</button>

Badge on Icons

Use .zak-badge-counter with a position: relative wrapper to anchor a count badge to an icon.

3
12
7
HTML
<div style="position: relative;">
  <svg class="zak-icon zak-icon-lg">...</svg>
  <span class="zak-badge zak-badge-danger zak-badge-counter">3</span>
</div>

Badge on Avatars

Anchor a count badge to an avatar using a relatively positioned wrapper.

JA 4
MK 9
HTML
<div style="position: relative;">
  <span class="zak-avatar zak-avatar-primary">JA</span>
  <span class="zak-badge zak-badge-success zak-badge-counter">4</span>
</div>

Dot Badge

.zak-badge-dot renders a standalone status dot.

Online Away Offline
HTML
<span class="zak-badge zak-badge-success zak-badge-dot"></span>
<span class="zak-badge zak-badge-warning zak-badge-dot"></span>
<span class="zak-badge zak-badge-danger zak-badge-dot"></span>

Badge Sizes

Adjust badge size with font-size utilities (badges scale from em-based padding).

Small Medium Large
HTML
<span class="zak-badge zak-badge-primary" style="font-size: 0.65rem;">Small</span>
<span class="zak-badge zak-badge-primary">Medium</span>
<span class="zak-badge zak-badge-primary" style="font-size: 0.95rem;">Large</span>

CSS Classes Reference

Class Description
.zak-badgeBase badge styling (neutral gray)
.zak-badge-primaryPrimary color variant
.zak-badge-successSuccess color variant
.zak-badge-dangerDanger color variant
.zak-badge-warningWarning color variant
.zak-badge-infoInfo color variant
.zak-badge-pillFully rounded pill shape
.zak-badge-dotCompact status dot
.zak-badge-counterAbsolute-positioned count anchored to top-right

Accessibility

  • Badges do not express semantic meaning by themselves — always combine a color variant with readable text.
  • Dot badges are decorative; pair them with a visible text label and add aria-hidden="true".
  • When a count badge is important (e.g. unread items), announce it with aria-label like "3 unread notifications".
  • Do not rely on color alone to convey state — text must always accompany the badge.
  • Counter badges on interactive elements should never intercept clicks; keep them non-interactive.
